title: Open-label placebos and prosocial behavior
summary: Placebo effects have been known for a long time. These are not only effective against physical pain, but also against psychological pain, e.g. when one feels socially excluded or empathically feels the pain of another person.  It is usually assumed that it is crucial for placebo effects that they are given in a concealed way. However, new studies show that even if subjects know that they are receiving a placebo, it can have an effect. This study aims to investigate whether these so-called open-label placebos can also reduce social and empathic pain.

interventions.name: Open-label placebo. Subjects are given a nasal spray, which is referred to as a placebo. Afterwards, the participants  look at pictures in which people are depicted in painful situations and we ask about their empathy with these people.
